claims.claim: Judging agents with the same accuracy before an environmental shift (base-rate guess, coincidental cue, ground-responsive) differ in how their judgement responds to interventions on the evidence and on the cue.
claims.rests_on: effect_E, effect_S (do(E), do(S)) and accuracy_pre_shift of the three conditions, 20 seeds, 95 % intervals not overlapping between the cue-driven and the evidence-driven conditions

claims.claim: The cue-driven agent loses accuracy when the cue decouples from the state; the ground-responsive agent does not.
claims.rests_on: shift_drop and stability_do_W (a balanced world with the cue decoupled)

claims.claim: With feedback on the true state the agent reconfigures its dependence (from the cue to the evidence); without feedback the dependence is kept.
claims.rests_on: revision_E, revision_S of 'correction and reconfiguration' against 'no correction'

claims.claim: An observation condition can change the record of a relation without changing the realized operation (scale, instrument noise, passive coupling, boundary, memory), and can change the operation itself (probe, environment, window).
claims.rests_on: compare_observations: the operation digest is identical for the first group and differs for the second

claims.claim: A shape of this domain carries the three weights of the agent's decision rule at the moment of the snapshot (plus sampling noise); before and after a moment at which the weights did not change, the shapes differ only by sampling noise.
claims.rests_on: construction.explain_shape: the fitted weights reproduce the recorded weights; construction.reading_of_difference

claims.claim: The pre-set operational criterion of the 'non-accidental core' (large effect of the evidence, small effect of the cue, stable correctness under do(W)) does not separate the miscalibrated misjudgement from the ground-responsive judgement.
claims.rests_on: attribution_tests: both NOT_NEGATED; the criterion tests responsiveness, not the correctness of the reading

claims.claim: The 'core-only' construction (response to the evidence alone) adds nothing over a static causal model of the same information on held-out interventions: REDUNDANT or HARMFUL in every condition.

No cut and no structural feature beyond a smooth ridge appears in the shapes of this domain: they are logistic surfaces of three weights, so the domain cannot show a richer 'operational shape' than the weights define.
claims.rests_on: explain_shape: cuts = 0 for the default conditions; the fit residual is at the sampling-noise level

claims.claim: Relations that were not detected (95 % interval includes 0) are not shown to be zero; relations an observation cannot identify are unresolved, not zero.
Non-accidentality is the characteristic core of a knowledge Gaisho (or of any Gaisho).
claims.rests_on: nothing: the laboratory reads candidate relations and does not assume a core; whether a core exists is not decided

claims.claim: The ground-responsive agent has a knowledge Gaisho; the cue-driven agent has an accidental one.
claims.rests_on: nothing: a synthetic operation has no bearer and no historical interval, and the attribution needs independent evidence

claims.claim: The operational criterion corresponds to what the manuscript GAISHO R37 means by the non-accidental core.
Ignition, maintenance, transformation, expiry and re-ignition of a Gaisho have the operational counterparts used here (feedback reconfiguration, shift, revision).
claims.rests_on: nothing: they are the laboratory's operationalisations, not R37's definitions

rules.cell: one cell per grid point (i, j) of the two interventions: nx x ny cells. It is RECORDED (a value from trials), or UNRESOLVED (a class of the reason it was not recorded): no cell is dropped.
rules.cell_value: the share of the trials of the cell that had the outcome, averaged over the seeds (one run per seed is the replication unit; the sd is across seeds).
rules.edge: one edge between two neighbouring grid points along an axis: (nx-1) x ny along the first axis plus nx x (ny-1) along the second, drawn only where both ends are RECORDED cells.
rules.cut: an edge whose two ends differ by at least 0.5 is a CUT: the surface is not drawn across it (a threshold of the laboratory, not a finding).
rules.branch_point: where the segment of an edge crosses the level 0.5 of the outcome (linear interpolation between the two recorded ends): a reconstructed relation, not a measured point.
rules.unresolved: a cell that was not recorded keeps its position on the base plane and the class of the reason (the six unobserved classes).
rules.projection: x and y are the intervention values, the height is the value of the cell: a VISUALIZATION_PROJECTION chosen by the laboratory and declared in the record; it is not a physical place.

construction.what_a_cell_is: the share of the trials of this cell with the outcome of the domain, when the two interventions are set to the values of the cell
construction.outcome_of_the_domain: the agent judges +1: P(J = +1 | do(E = x), do(S = y)) = sigmoid(a x + b y + c) with the agent's weights (a, b, c) at the moment of the snapshot, estimated by the share of n trials per cell. It is the response of the agent's decision rule to the two interventions, not the correctness of its judgement.

what_the_surface_carries.reading: the recorded cells are reproduced by three numbers, the weights of the agent's decision rule at this moment, up to sampling noise: the surface is a reading of that rule under intervention. It is not a record of the run's history and nothing in it is a Gaisho; its form (a logistic ridge) is a property of the model's decision rule, so a difference between two shapes of this domain is a difference of those weights (or of sampling noise).
